vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: tidyup
Version: 2.0.0

The TidyUp skill is a simple Bash-based activity logger designed to track manual disk maintenance tasks. While the description in SKILL.md suggests it 'finds duplicates' and 'reclaims space,' the actual implementation in scripts/script.sh is limited to appending user-provided strings to local log files in ~/.local/share/tidyup/ and providing basic search/export functionality. No network access, data exfiltration, or malicious execution patterns were found.

llm.summary: The manifest and SKILL.md promise duplicate-finding and cleanup, but the provided script only implements a local logging/recording/export utility — no scanning, deduplication, or deletion — so the skill's stated purpose does not match what it actually does.
llm.guidance: The skill's public description promises duplicate-finding and cleanup, but the included code is only a local logging/export utility — it does not scan, identify duplicates, or delete files. If you install or run this, expect plain-text logs stored at ~/.local/share/tidyup; no network access or credentials are requested. Before using: (1) review the script yourself if you can; (2) be cautious about logging any sensitive strings (entries are stored unencrypted); (3) note the JSON export has bugs and may produce invalid JSON or unescaped values; (4) if you want actual duplicate detection or automated cleanup, use a dedicated tool (fdupes, rmlint, find + md5/sha hashing) rather than this logger; (5) check and, if desired, restrict permissions on ~/.local/share/tidyup, and remove the script if you don't want persistent local logs.
